name: NGC 1637 Cepheid 54700
description: A Cepheid in the galaxy NGC 1637 that pulsates every 54.4 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 54.42 d in Leonard et al. (2003), ApJ 594, 247, table 8 (ID 54700: P 54.42 d); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 54.42 d in Leonard et al. (2003), ApJ 594, 247, table 8 (ID 54700: P 54.42 d); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of NGC 1637, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2004MNRAS.350.1195M; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in NGC 1637 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 9,289,203 pc (src/objects/ngc-1637-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 9,289,664 pc, inclination 31.1 deg, line of nodes 20.6 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Jones2009ApJ...696.1176J: Distance Determination to 12 Type II Supernovae Using the Expanding Photosphere Method (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2009ApJ...696.1176J); catalogue reference Jones2009ApJ...696.1176J: 9289663.8678 pc (-458864.863614/+482708.341758); sn

position.credit: Leonard et al. (2003), ApJ 594, 247, table 6 (ID 54700: chip 4, X 414.8, Y 216.8); its section 4.1 says the hstphot positions it reports are of the combined V-band frame, which no epoch leaves by more than about half a pixel, and that hstphot gives an integer to a star centred on a pixel's lower-left corner; read here on the first exposure of that series, u6fv0101m (table 3)

text.card: A Cepheid in the galaxy NGC 1637, 9.3 million parsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 54.4 days.
text.introduction: Leonard et al. (2003) list its pulsation at 54.4 days. It is one of the 18 Cepheids their distance to the galaxy rests on.
text.locator: table 8, ID 54700: P, and note a

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within NGC 1637 is not measured
